exam.title: 2019年全国硕士研究生招生考试英语（二）真题

passages.title: Section I: Use of English
passages.content:
Weighing yourself regularly is a wonderful way to stay aware of any significant weight fluctuations. [1], when done too often, this habit can sometimes hurt more than it [2].

As for me, weighing myself every day caused me to shift my focus from being generally healthy and physically active, to focusing [3] on the scale. That was bad to my overall fitness goals. I had gained weight in the form of muscle mass, but thinking only of [4] the number on the scale, I altered my training program. That conflicted with how I needed to train to [5] my goals.

I also found that weighing myself daily did not provide an accurate [6] of the hard work and progress I was making in the gym. It takes about three weeks to a month to notice significant changes in your weight [7] altering your training program. The most [8] changes will be observed in skill level, strength and inches lost.

For these [9], I stopped weighing myself every day and switched to a bimonthly weighing schedule [10]. Since weight loss is not my goal, it is less important for me to [11] my weight each week. Weighing every other week allows me to observe and [12] any significant weight changes. That tells me whether I need to [13] my training program.

I use my bimonthly weigh-in [14] to get information about my nutrition as well. If my training intensity remains the same, but I'm constantly [15] and dropping weight, this is a [16] that I need to increase my daily caloric intake.

The [17] to stop weighing myself every day has done wonders for my overall health, fitness and well-being. I'm experiencing increased zeal for working out since I no longer carry the burden of a [18] morning weigh-in. I've also experienced greater success in achieving my specific fitness goals, [19] I'm training according to those goals, not the numbers on a scale.

Rather than [20] over the scale, turn your focus to how you look, feel, how your clothes fit and your overall energy level.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 1
passages.content:
Unlike so-called basic emotions such as sadness, fear, and anger, guilt emerges a little later, in conjunction with a child's growing grasp of social and moral norms. Children aren't born knowing how to say "I'm sorry"; rather, they learn over time that such statements appease parents and friends — and their own consciences. This is why researchers generally regard so-called moral guilt, in the right amount, to be a good thing.

In the popular imagination, of course, guilt still gets a bad rap. It is deeply uncomfortable — it's the emotional equivalent of wearing a jacket weighted with stones. Yet this understanding is outdated. "There has been a kind of revival or a rethinking about what guilt is and what role guilt can serve," says Amrisha Vaish, a psychology researcher at the University of Virginia, adding that this revival is part of a larger recognition that emotions aren't binary — feelings that may be advantageous in one context may be harmful in another. Jealousy and anger, for example, may have evolved to alert us to important inequalities. Too much happiness can be destructive.

And guilt, by prompting us to think more deeply about our goodness, can encourage humans to make up for errors and fix relationships. Guilt, in other words, can help hold a cooperative species together. It is a kind of social glue.

Viewed in this light, guilt is an opportunity. Work by Tina Malti, a psychology professor at the University of Toronto, suggests that guilt may compensate for an emotional deficiency. In a number of studies, Malti and others have shown that guilt and sympathy may represent different pathways to cooperation and sharing. Some kids who are low in sympathy may make up for that shortfall by experiencing more guilt, which can rein in their nastier impulses. And vice versa: High sympathy can substitute for low guilt.

In a 2014 study, for example, Malti looked at 244 children. Using caregiver assessments and the children's self-observations, she rated each child's overall sympathy level and his or her tendency to feel negative emotions after moral transgressions. Then the kids were handed chocolate coins, and given a chance to share them with an anonymous child. For the low-sympathy kids, how much they shared appeared to turn on how inclined they were to feel guilty. The guilt-prone ones shared more, even though they hadn't magically become more sympathetic to the other child's deprivation.

"That's good news," Malti says. "We can be prosocial because we caused harm and we feel regret."

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 2
passages.content:
Forests give us shade, quiet and one of the harder challenges in the fight against climate change. Even as we humans count on forests to soak up a good share of the carbon dioxide we produce, we are threatening their ability to do so. The climate change we are hastening could one day leave us with forests that emit more carbon than they absorb.

Thankfully, there is a way out of this trap — but it involves striking a subtle balance. Helping forests flourish as valuable "carbon sinks" long into the future may require reducing their capacity to absorb carbon now. California is leading the way, as it does on so many climate efforts, in figuring out the details.

The state's proposed Forest Carbon Plan aims to double efforts to thin out young trees and clear brush in parts of the forest. This temporarily lowers carbon-carrying capacity. But the remaining trees draw a greater share of the available moisture, so they grow and thrive, restoring the forest's capacity to pull carbon from the air. Healthy trees are also better able to fend off insects. The landscape is rendered less easily burnable. Even in the event of a fire, fewer trees are consumed.

The need for such planning is increasingly urgent. Already, since 2010, drought and insects have killed over 100 million trees in California, most of them in 2016 alone, and wildfires have burned hundreds of thousands of acres.

California plans to treat 35,000 acres of forest a year by 2020, and 60,000 by 2030 — financed from the proceeds of the state's emissions-permit auctions. That's only a small share of the total acreage that could benefit, about half a million acres in all, so it will be vital to prioritize areas at greatest risk of fire or drought.

The strategy also aims to ensure that carbon in woody material removed from the forests is locked away in the form of solid lumber or burned as biofuel in vehicles that would otherwise run on fossil fuels. New research on transportation biofuels is already under way.

State governments are well accustomed to managing forests, but traditionally they've focused on wildlife, watersheds and opportunities for recreation. Only recently have they come to see the vital part forests will have to play in storing carbon. California's plan, which is expected to be finalized by the governor next year, should serve as a model.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 3
passages.content:
American farmers have been complaining of labor shortages for several years. The complaints are unlikely to stop without an overhaul of immigration rules for farm workers.

Congress has obstructed efforts to create a more straightforward visa for agricultural workers that would let foreign workers stay longer in the U.S. and change jobs within the industry. If this doesn't change, American businesses, communities, and consumers will be the losers.

Perhaps half of U.S. farm laborers are undocumented immigrants. As fewer such workers enter the country, the characteristics of the agricultural workforce are changing. Today's farm laborers, while still predominantly born in Mexico, are more likely to be settled rather than migrating and more likely to be married than single. They're also aging. At the start of this century, about one-third of crop workers were over the age of 35. Now more than half are. And picking crops is hard on older bodies. One oft-debated cure for this labor shortage remains as implausible as it's been all along: Native U.S. workers won't be returning to the farm.

Mechanization isn't the answer, either — not yet, at least. Production of corn, cotton, rice, soybeans, and wheat has been largely mechanized, but many high-value, labor-intensive crops, such as strawberries, need labor. Even dairy farms, where robots do a small share of milking, have a long way to go before they're automated.

As a result, farms have grown increasingly reliant on temporary guest workers using the H-2A visa to fill the gaps in the workforce. Starting around 2012, requests for the visas rose sharply; from 2011 to 2016 the number of visas issued more than doubled. The H-2A visa has no numerical cap, unlike the H-2B visa for nonagricultural work, which is limited to 66,000 a year. Even so, employers complain they aren't given all the workers they need. The process is cumbersome, expensive, and unreliable. One survey found that bureaucratic delays led the average H-2A worker to arrive on the job 22 days late. The shortage is compounded by federal immigration raids, which remove some workers and drive others underground.

In a 2012 survey, 71 percent of tree-fruit growers and almost 80 percent of raisin and berry growers said they were short of labor. Some western farmers have responded by moving operations to Mexico. From 1998 to 2000, 14.5 percent of the fruit Americans consumed was imported. Little more than a decade later, the share of imports was 25.8 percent.

In effect, the U.S. can import food or it can import the workers who pick it.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 4
passages.content:
Arnold Schwarzenegger, Dia Mirza and Adrian Grenier have a message for you: It's easy to beat plastic. They're part of a bunch of celebrities starring in a new video for World Environment Day — encouraging you, the consumer, to swap out your single-use plastic staples like straws and cutlery to combat the plastics crisis.

The key messages that have been put together for World Environment Day do include a call for governments to enact legislation to curb single-use plastics. But the overarching message is directed at individuals.

My concern with leaving it up to the individual, however, is our limited sense of what needs to be achieved. On their own, taking our own bags to the grocery store or quitting plastic straws, for example, will accomplish little and require very little of us. They could even be detrimental, satisfying a need to have "done our bit" without ever progressing onto bigger, bolder, more effective actions — a kind of "moral licensing" that allays our concerns and stops us doing more and asking more of those in charge.

While the conversation around our environment and our responsibility toward it remains centered on shopping bags and straws, we're ignoring the balance of power that implies that as "consumers" we must shop sustainably, rather than as "citizens" hold our governments and industries to account to push for real systemic change.

It's important to acknowledge that the environment isn't everyone's priority — or even most people's. We shouldn't expect it to be. In her latest book, Why Good People Do Bad Environmental Things, Wellesley College professor Elizabeth R. DeSombre argues that the best way to collectively change the behavior of large numbers of people is for the change to be structural.

This might mean implementing policy such as a plastic tax that adds a cost to environmentally problematic action, or banning single-use plastics altogether. India has just announced it will "eliminate all single-use plastic in the country by 2022." There are also incentive-based ways of making better environmental choices easier, such as ensuring recycling is at least as easy as trash disposal.

DeSombre isn't saying people should stop caring about the environment. It's just that individual actions are too slow, she says, for that to be the only, or even primary, approach to changing widespread behavior.

None of this is about writing off the individual. It's just about putting things into perspective. We don't have time to wait. We need progressive policies that shape collective action (and rein in polluting businesses), alongside engaged citizens pushing for change.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part B
passages.content:
In choosing a new home, Camille McClain's kids have a single demand: a backyard.

McClain's little ones aren't the only kids who have an opinion when it comes to housing, and in many cases youngsters' views weigh heavily on parents' real estate decisions, according to a 2018 Harris Poll survey of more than 2,000 U.S. adults.

While more families buck an older-generation proclivity to leave kids in the dark about real estate decisions, realty agents and psychologists have mixed views about the financial, personal and long-term effects kids' opinions may have.

The idea of involving children in a big decision is a great idea because it can help them feel a sense of control and ownership in what can be an overwhelming process, said Ryan Hooper, a clinical psychologist in Chicago.

"Children may face serious difficulties in coping with significant moves, especially if it removes them from their current school or support system," he said.

Greg Jaroszewski, a real estate broker with Gagliardo Realty Associates, said he's not convinced that kids should be involved in selecting a home — but their opinions should be considered in regards to proximity to friends and social activities, if possible.

Younger children should feel like they're choosing their home — without actually getting a choice in the matter, said Adam Bailey, a real estate attorney based in New York.

Asking them questions about what they like about the backyard of a potential home will make them feel like they're being included in the decision-making process, Bailey said.

Many of the aspects of homebuying aren't a consideration for children, said Tracey Hampson, a real estate agent based in Santa Clarita, Calif. And placing too much emphasis on their opinions can ruin a fantastic home purchase.

"Speaking with your children before you make a real estate decision is wise, but I wouldn't base the purchasing decision solely on their opinions," Hampson said.

The other issue is that many children — especially older ones — may base their real estate knowledge on HGTV shows, said Aaron Norris of The Norris Group in Riverside, Calif.

"They love Chip and Joanna Gaines just as much as the rest of us," he said. "HGTV has seriously changed how people view real estate. It's not shelter, it's a lifestyle. With that mindset change come some serious money consequences."

Kids tend to get stuck in the features and the immediate benefits to them personally, Norris said.

Parents need to remind their children that their needs and desires may change over time, said Julie Gurner, a real estate analyst with FitSmallBusiness.com.

"Their opinions can change tomorrow," Gurner said. "Harsh as it may be to say, that decision should likely not be made contingent on a child's opinions, but rather made for them with great consideration into what home can meet their needs best — and give them an opportunity to customize it a bit and make it their own."

This advice is more relevant now than ever before, even as more parents want to embrace the ideas of their children, despite the current housing crunch.

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [1] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句间逻辑关系与副词辨析。

［解题思路］首句指出定期称重是随时了解体重波动的极佳方式（a wonderful way）；次句指出如果称重过于频繁，这一习惯造成的伤害有时会大于益处。前句赞扬其益处，后句指出其弊端，两句之间存在明显的转折对比关系，故正确答案为［D］However（然而）。

［错项排除］［A］Besides（此外）表递进补充；［B］Therefore（因此）表因果结果；［C］Otherwise（否则）表相反假设条件，三项均无法体现转折关系。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [2] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］动词语义辨析与比较结构搭配。

［解题思路］空格所在分句hurt more than it [2]与首句中的a wonderful way形成语义照应，hurt（伤害）与空格词形成鲜明反义对比。能与hurt相对立并构成比较的是表示“有帮助、有益处”的词，故选［A］helps（帮助，促进）。hurt more than it helps意为“弊大于利、害多于益”。

［错项排除］［B］cares（关心，照料）；［C］warns（警告，提醒）；［D］reduces（减少，降低），三项均不能与hurt形成对仗反义搭配。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [3] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］副词语义辨析与语境限制。

［解题思路］第二段开头作者结合自身经历指出，每日称重导致自己将注意力从“保持整体健康和运动活力”转移到“只关注体重计上的数字”。后句强调thinking only of the number，only与［B］solely（仅仅，单独地）形成精准语义同义复现，故选［B］。

［错项排除］［A］initially（最初，首先）；［C］occasionally（偶尔）；［D］formally（形式上，正式地），均无法体现“唯独、极端局限”的负面偏狭语境。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [4] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］动词辨析与动宾搭配。

［解题思路］作者指出自己通过锻炼增加了肌肉重量（gained weight in the form of muscle mass），但因为心中只想着“让体重计上的数字降下来”，从而错误地修改了训练计划。数字下降对应［B］lowering（降低，减少），lowering the number on the scale符合语境。

［错项排除］［A］recording（记录）；［C］explaining（解释）；［D］accepting（接受），均无法体现盲目减重、排斥肌肉增长数字的心态。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [5] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］动宾搭配与目标达成。
［解题思路］第二段末句指出，错误调整后的训练计划与自己为了“实现目标（reach my goals）”所需采用的训练方式产生了冲突。reach one's goals 为英语最地道高频搭配，意为“达成目标”，与上文 overall fitness goals 呼应，故选[D]。
［错项排除］[A] modify（修改）与[B] set（设定）在前文均已完成目标设立背景下的行动阶段，此处强调训练目的是实现已定目标；[C] review（审视、回顾）同样不符通过训练兑现目标的语义。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [6] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］名词辨析与语境对应。

［解题思路］作者第三段指出，每日称重并不能准确反映出自己在健身房付出的辛勤努力与进步。provide an accurate depiction of...意为“准确描绘/真实反映出……”，depiction（描绘，刻画，反映）切中文意，故选［B］。

［错项排除］［A］definition（定义）；［C］distribution（分配，分布）；［D］prediction（预测），三项均不符合“体现训练成效”的搭配语义。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [7] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］介词短语辨析与因果逻辑。

［解题思路］空格前后为：在改变训练计划之后，需要大约三周到一个多月才能察觉到体重的显著变化。空格后altering your training program是体重变化的原因，due to表示“由于，归因于”，引导原因状语，故选［A］due to。

［错项排除］［B］regardless of（不管，不顾）；［C］aside from（除了……之外）；［D］along with（随着，与……一道），均无法表达因果因由。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [8] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］形容词辨析与时间语义对比。

［解题思路］上文提到体重数字的变化需要数周到一个月才能体现，而技能水平、力量增长和体围缩小则是最先、最快被观察到的。immediate在此表示“立即的，最直接的”，与上文需漫长等待的体重变化形成时间快慢对照，故选［D］immediate。

［错项排除］［A］orderly（整齐的，有秩序的）；［B］rigid（死板的，僵硬的）；［C］precise（精确的），均无法体现“立竿见影、迅速显现”的含义。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [9] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］固定搭配与段落因果过渡。
［解题思路］第四段首句承接前两段剖析的每日称重弊端，作者总结道：出于以上这些原因（For these reasons），我停止每天称重。for these reasons 是英语中最经典的承前启后总结短语，指代前文只关注数字等一系列教训，故选[C]。
［错项排除］[A] claims（主张、声称）、[B] judgments（判断）与[D] methods（方法）均不能与前面阐述的原因构成自然合理的因果总结搭配。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [10] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］副词辨析与行为方式切换。
［解题思路］第四段首句指出自己停止了每日称重，转而改用每两周一次的称重频率（switched to a bimonthly weighing schedule [10]）。副词 instead 置于句尾，意为“相反、作为替代”，精准凸显摒弃错误旧习、采取全新频率的转变，故选[A]。
［错项排除］[B] though（虽然、然而，多表语气弱转折让步）；[C] again（再次）与改变频率的初次切换不符；[D] indeed（确实）表递进肯定，均不能准确刻画“舍甲取乙”的替代关系。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [11] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］动词词义与健康监测固定搭配。
［解题思路］第四段首句表明作者改为每两周称重一次，第二句紧接着指出：既然减重不是我的目标，那么每周去“记录、追踪（track）”体重就显得不那么重要了。track my weight 意为“持续追踪体重变化”，符合定期自我监测身体数据曲线的语境，并与下句 observe and record 呼应，故选［A］。
［错项排除］［B］overlook（忽视、忽略）和［C］conceal（隐藏、隐瞒）语义方向与收集体重信息相反；［D］report（汇报、报告）常用于向他人呈报，个人日常健身记录无需每周汇报。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [12] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］动词短语辨析与原因解释。

［解题思路］每隔一周称重一次允许我观察并查明（account for）任何显著的体重变化。account for在此意为“对……做出合理解释，弄清……的原因”，与observe形成并列递进：先观察到变化，再分析其原因，故选［D］account for。

［错项排除］［A］depend on（取决于）；［B］approve of（赞同）；［C］hold onto（坚守，保住），均不能与体重变化搭配表达分析溯源。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [13] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］动宾搭配与语境连贯性。
［解题思路］第四段末句指出：观察并弄清显著的体重变化，能够告诉我是否需要对训练计划进行调整（[13] my training program）。adjust 意为“调整、微调”，准确呼应第二段因误判而草率修改（altered）训练计划的正反对照，故选[B]。
［错项排除］[A] share（分享）、[C] confirm（确认）与[D] prepare（准备）均不能体现依据身体反馈灵活改良已有计划的含义。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [14] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］名词词义辨析与称重信息采集。
［解题思路］第五段首句指出：我还利用每半月一次的称重“结果、数据（results）”来获取有关营养状况的信息（to get information about my nutrition）。weigh-in results 指每次站上体重秤测得的客观数字结果，顺承下文根据体重下降来调整每日热量摄入的反馈机制，故选［A］。
［错项排除］［B］features（特征、特点）和［C］rules（规则、条例）均无法直接量化产出营养摄入信息；［D］tests（测试）与前置定语 weigh-in（称重测试）在语义上重复，不构成动宾合理搭配。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [15] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］形容词辨析与身体生理反应。

［解题思路］下文指出“需要增加日常热量摄入（increase my daily caloric intake）”，这说明身体能量摄入不足，因此生理状态必然是经常感到“饥饿”，hungry and dropping weight（经常挨饿且体重不断下滑）完全契合，故选［C］hungry。

［错项排除］［A］bored（无聊的）；［B］anxious（焦虑的）；［D］sick（生病的），均无法作为提示“必须增加卡路里摄入”的直接营养反馈指标。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [16] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］名词辨析与生理预警信号表达。
［解题思路］第五段第二句指出：如果我的训练强度保持不变，但我经常感到饥饿且体重持续下降，这就是一个明确的“迹象/信号（sign）”，表明我需要增加日常卡路里摄入量。a sign that... 为固定同位语结构，意为“显示……的征兆或信号”，契合身体发出的客观营养预警，故选［D］。
［错项排除］［A］principle（原则、原理）、［B］secret（秘密）以及［C］belief（信念、看法）均带主观色彩或属抽象准则，无法指代饥饿和掉秤释放出的客观信号。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [17] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］名词辨析与自主行动抉择。
［解题思路］第六段首句总结全篇核心举措：停止每日称重的这一“决定（decision）”对我的整体健康、体能水平和幸福感产生了极大益处（has done wonders）。the decision to stop weighing myself 紧扣第四段作者主动放弃每日称重、转向双周日程的关键选择，故选［C］。
［错项排除］［A］request（请求）多指对他人提出要求；［B］necessity（必需品、必要性）未能体现个人主动取舍；［D］wish（愿望）仅停留在主观意愿层面，尚未转化为实际行动与成效。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [18] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］形容词辨析与心理重负照应。

［解题思路］作者表示自己对健身产生了更大的热情，因为不再背负每天早晨称重带来的令人沮丧失望的心理负担（burden of a disappointing morning weigh-in）。disappointing符合人们每日面对数字波动时的沮丧心态，故选［A］disappointing。

［错项排除］［B］surprising（令人吃惊的）；［C］restricting（限制性的）；［D］consuming（消耗性的），均无法贴切修饰打击健身信心的称重心理负担。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [19] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］连词辨析与句间因果逻辑论证。
［解题思路］第六段末句指出：我在实现具体健身目标方面也取得了更大成功，因为（because）我现在是依据那些切实的健身目标而非体重计上的冰冷数字来进行训练的。后半句直接揭示了前文“取得更大成功”的根本原因，构成前果后因的逻辑论证，故选［D］。
［错项排除］［A］if（如果）和［B］unless（除非）均引导条件状语从句，表示假设前提；［C］until（直到……为止）引导时间状语从句，三者均无法解释已然实现的成功结果背后的原因。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [20] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］动词短语辨析与警示呼吁。

［解题思路］末段作者向读者呼吁：与其对体重计上的数字过度执迷（obsessing over the scale），不如将精力转向自己的外表容貌、感觉、衣服合身度以及整体精力水平。obsess over意为“对……过分挂念/执迷不悟”，与后半句积极豁达的心态形成强烈对比，选［A］obsessing。

［错项排除］［B］dominating（主导，支配）；［C］puzzling（使迷惑）；［D］triumphing（战胜，获胜），三项均无法与over搭配表达沉溺执迷之态。

questions.stem: Researchers think that guilt can be a good thing because it may help
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］因果细节题（考查研究人员认为内疚感是好事的原因）。

［解题思路］首段①句指出内疚感是随着孩子对社会和道德规范的逐步领会而出现的（in conjunction with a child's growing grasp of social and moral norms）；②句说明孩子表达道歉有助于安抚他人以及自身的良知；③句得出结论This is why researchers generally regard so-called moral guilt... to be a good thing。因此研究人员认为适度内疚是好事的原因在于它能够促进儿童道德品质的发展，［C］foster a child's moral development正确。

［错项排除］［A］调节基础情绪混淆概念，内疚与基础情绪是发展阶段的比较而非调节关系；［B］提升智力无中生有；［D］强化积极情感与适度内疚的道德指南针功能相悖。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 2, many people still consider guilt to be
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］事实细节题（考查公众传统观念中对内疚感的看法）。

［解题思路］第二段前两句指出：在公众印象中，内疚感名声不佳（gets a bad rap），它让人极度不适，“就像穿了一件装满石头的沉重外套”（the emotional equivalent of wearing a jacket weighted with stones）。jacket weighted with stones形象比喻沉重的情感负担，［B］burdensome（沉重的，繁重的）为此比喻的同义提炼，故选［B］。

［错项排除］［A］deceptive（欺骗性的）；［C］addictive（令人上瘾的）；［D］inexcusable（不可原谅的），均与“如负巨石”的沉重感无关。

questions.stem: Vaish holds that the rethinking about guilt comes from an awareness that

options.text: an emotion can play opposing roles
options.content: an emotion can play opposing roles

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］观点态度题（考查学者Vaish对内疚感反思根源的认识）。

［解题思路］第二段中Vaish指出对内疚感的新反思属于心理学领域保护人们免受负面情绪影响趋势的一部分，她指出情绪并非非黑即白，而是取决于具体语境：emotions aren't binary — feelings that may be advantageous in one context may be harmful in another（情绪并非二元对立——在某种语境下有益的情绪在另一种语境下可能有害）。同一种情绪在不同语境下可发挥相反作用，［D］an emotion can play opposing roles 准确同义转换了 advantageous in one context / harmful in another，故选［D］。

［错项排除］［A］情绪与语境无关与原文depending on the context直接相悖；［B］强调情绪具社会建设性仅局限于正面，遗漏了有益与无益的辩证对比；［C］情绪稳定有利于健康偏离文本论述核心。

questions.stem: Malti and others have shown that cooperation and sharing

options.text: can result from either sympathy or guilt
options.content: can result from either sympathy or guilt

options.text: may be the outcome of impulsive acts
options.content: may be the outcome of impulsive acts

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］事实细节题（考查学者Malti关于合作与分享行为的研究发现）。

［解题思路］第四段③句明确指出：Malti and others have shown that guilt and sympathy may represent different pathways to cooperation and sharing（马尔蒂等人指出，内疚感和同情心代表了通向合作与分享的不同路径）。有的孩子靠同情，有的孩子靠内疚，两者皆可激发合作与分享行为，［B］can result from either sympathy or guilt切中文意，故选［B］。

［错项排除］［A］纠正情绪缺陷与后文互补代偿机制不符；［C］带来情感满足颠倒了因果逻辑；［D］冲动行为的产物与理性道德情感的引导相反。

questions.stem: The word "transgressions" (Line 4, Para. 5) is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］词义句意题（考查代词语境与词汇含义推断）。

［解题思路］划线词位于第五段②句：In a 2014 study, for example, Malti looked at 244 children... she rated each child's overall sympathy level and his or her tendency to feel negative emotions after moral transgressions（马尔蒂评估了孩子整体的同情心水平及其在面临道德越轨行为后的负面情绪倾向）。后文第六段末句进一步通过孩子所犯错误解释道：guilt tells them, we caused harm and we feel regret（内疚感告诉他们：我们造成了伤害，我们感到后悔）。造成伤害、引发违背道德良知的行为即为道德越轨/过错，transgressions在此即指wrongdoings（违法行为，过失，过错），故选［D］。

［错项排除］［A］teachings（教导）；［B］discussions（讨论）；［C］restrictions（限制），均与道德过失行为的含义相差甚远。

questions.stem: By saying "one of the harder challenges", the author implies that

options.text: global climate change may get out of control
options.content: global climate change may get out of control

options.text: forests may become a potential threat
options.content: forests may become a potential threat

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］推理判断题（第一段）。
［解题思路］第一段首句指出森林给了我们绿荫、宁静，也是抗击气候变化过程中最棘手的挑战之一（one of the harder challenges）。紧接着后两句解释：人类指望森林吸收大量二氧化碳，却正威胁其这一能力；加速中的气候变化有朝一日可能使森林排放的碳多于吸收的碳（emit more carbon than they absorb）。这暗示本该吸收碳的森林未来可能反过来成为气候问题的潜在威胁，故 [D] forests may become a potential threat 正确。
［错项排除］[A] global climate change may get out of control 过度绝对化；[B] people may misunderstand global warming 与民众误解无关；[C] extreme weather conditions may arise 仅笼统泛指极端天气，未切中森林“角色逆转成威胁”的深层隐忧。

questions.stem: To maintain forests as valuable "carbon sinks", we may need to

options.text: preserve the diversity of species in them
options.content: preserve the diversity of species in them

options.text: accelerate the growth of young trees
options.content: accelerate the growth of young trees

options.text: strike a balance among different plants
options.content: strike a balance among different plants

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］事实细节题（第二段）。
［解题思路］第二段明确指出：“Helping forests flourish as valuable 'carbon sinks' long into the future may require reducing their capacity to absorb carbon now.”（要帮助森林在长远未来继续作为宝贵的“碳汇”茁壮成长，现在可能需要降低其吸碳能力。）选项 [D] lower their present carbon-absorbing capacity 是对 reducing their capacity to absorb carbon now 的精准同义改写，故选 [D]。
［错项排除］[A] preserve the diversity of species in them（保护物种多样性）、[B] accelerate the growth of young trees（加速幼树生长——恰恰相反，下段倡导疏伐幼树 thin out young trees）与[C] strike a balance among different plants（在植物间取得平衡——偷换原文的“长期与短期平衡”）均偏离原意。

questions.stem: California's Forest Carbon Plan endeavors to

options.text: reduce the density of some of its forests
options.content: reduce the density of some of its forests

options.text: find more effective ways to kill insects
options.content: find more effective ways to kill insects

options.text: restore its forests quickly after wildfires
options.content: restore its forests quickly after wildfires

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］事实细节题（第三段）。
［解题思路］第三段首句指出：“The state's proposed Forest Carbon Plan aims to double efforts to thin out young trees and clear brush in parts of the forest.”（该州提议的森林碳计划旨在加倍努力对部分林区进行疏伐幼树和清理灌木丛。）疏伐多余幼树与灌木丛以让留存树木充分汲取水分并降低可燃性，本质上就是降低部分森林的树木密度，故选 [B] reduce the density of some of its forests。
［错项排除］[A] cultivate more drought-resistant trees（培育抗旱树种）、[C] find more effective ways to kill insects（寻找更有效杀虫方法——健康大树自然能抵御虫害）与[D] restore its forests quickly after wildfires（火后快速恢复——计划旨在事先预防大火而非灾后补救）均属曲解。

questions.stem: What is essential to California's plan according to Paragraph 5?

options.text: To handle the areas in serious danger first.
options.content: To handle the areas in serious danger first.

options.text: To carry it out before the year of 2020.
options.content: To carry it out before the year of 2020.

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］事实细节题（第五段）。
［解题思路］第五段（即加州计划具体落地段）指出：“That's only a small share of the total acreage that could benefit, about half a million acres in all, so it will be vital to prioritize areas at greatest risk of fire or drought.”（这只是可受益总面积的一小部分，因此优先处理火灾或干旱风险最大的区域将至关重要。）其中 prioritize areas at greatest risk 与 [A] To handle the areas in serious danger first 完美同义对应，故选 [A]。
［错项排除］[B] To carry it out before the year of 2020 曲解了“by 2020 每年处理 3.5 万英亩”的阶段指标；[C] To perfect the emissions-permit auctions 将“从碳排放配额拍卖收益获得资金”偷换为完善拍卖制度本身；[D] To obtain enough financial support 偏离了本段强调空间优先级分配的核心重点（vital to prioritize）。

questions.stem: The author's attitude to California's plan can best be described as
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］观点态度题（第二段及末段）。
［解题思路］作者在第二段称赞加州在这方面走在前列（California is leading the way），并在末段末句给出明确正面评价：“California's plan, which is expected to be finalized by the governor next year, should serve as a model.”（加州的计划应当成为一个典范。）这充分表明作者对加州森林碳计划持明确的支持肯定态度，故选 [C] supportive。
［错项排除］[A] ambiguous（含糊不清的）、[B] tolerant（容忍的，带有保留或勉强认可意味）与[D] cautious（谨慎的）均与称赞加州“领先并堪称典范”的鲜明赞许基调不符。

questions.stem: What problem should be addressed according to the first two paragraphs?

options.text: Discrimination against foreign workers in the U.S.
options.content: Discrimination against foreign workers in the U.S.

options.text: Biased laws in favor of some American businesses.
options.content: Biased laws in favor of some American businesses.

options.text: Flaws in U.S. immigration rules for farm workers.
options.content: Flaws in U.S. immigration rules for farm workers.

options.text: Decline of job opportunities in U.S. agriculture.
options.content: Decline of job opportunities in U.S. agriculture.

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］事实细节题（第一、二段）。
［解题思路］第一段指出：“The complaints are unlikely to stop without an overhaul of immigration rules for farm workers.”（不对农工移民法规进行彻底改革，抱怨就不会停止。）第二段紧接着批评国会阻挠建立更简明高效的农业工人签证制度。由此可知亟待解决的问题在于美国农工移民法规存在的缺陷，故选 [C] Flaws in U.S. immigration rules for farm workers。
［错项排除］[A] Discrimination against foreign workers in the U.S.（对外国工人的歧视）无中生有；[B] Biased laws in favor of some American businesses（偏袒部分美企的法律）曲解了立法阻碍导致美国企业成输家（will be the losers）；[D] Decline of job opportunities in U.S. agriculture（美国农业工作机会减少）与面临严重用工荒相反。

questions.stem: One trouble with U.S. agricultural workforce is

options.text: the rising number of illegal immigrants
options.content: the rising number of illegal immigrants

options.text: the high mobility of crop workers
options.content: the high mobility of crop workers

options.text: the aging of immigrant farm workers
options.content: the aging of immigrant farm workers

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］事实细节题（第三段）。
［解题思路］第三段剖析了美国农业劳动力的结构性变化：“They're also aging. At the start of this century, about one-third of crop workers were over the age of 35. Now more than half are. And picking crops is hard on older bodies.” 目前过半农工超过35岁且劳力不断老化，难以胜任繁重的田间采摘工作，即面临移民农工老龄化困境，故选 [D] the aging of immigrant farm workers。
［错项排除］[A] the rising number of illegal immigrants 与首句后半部分“As fewer such workers enter the country（进入的非法移民越来越少）”完全相反；[B] the high mobility of crop workers 与“more likely to be settled rather than migrating（更有可能定居而非四处迁徙）”相悖；[C] the lack of experienced laborers 混淆了年龄老化与缺乏经验。

questions.stem: What is the much-argued solution to the labor shortage in U.S. farming?

options.text: To attract younger laborers to farm work.
options.content: To attract younger laborers to farm work.

options.text: To get native U.S. workers back to farming.
options.content: To get native U.S. workers back to farming.

options.text: To use more robots to grow high-value crops.
options.content: To use more robots to grow high-value crops.

options.text: To strengthen financial support for farmers.
options.content: To strengthen financial support for farmers.

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］事实细节题（考查解决美国农业劳动力短缺中备受争议的方案）。

［解题思路］原文第三段末句明确指出：One oft-debated cure for this labor shortage remains as implausible as it's been all along: Native U.S. workers won't be returning to the farm.（针对这一劳动力短缺问题，有一个屡被争论但始终不切实际的解决对策：美国本土工人不会重返农场。）其中 oft-debated cure（备受争论的对策）精确对应题干中的 much-argued solution，［B］To get native U.S. workers back to farming.（让美国本土工人重返农业劳动）与之完全一致，故［B］正确。

［错项排除］［A］“吸引年轻劳动力从事农业”在原文未提及，第三段仅描述现有农工老龄化；［C］“用更多机器人种植高价值作物”被第四段明确否定为“尚需时日”；［D］“加强对农民的财政支持”无中生有，故排除。

questions.stem: Agricultural employers complain about the H-2A visa for its
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］事实细节题（第五段）。
［解题思路］第五段（即 H-2A 签证段）指出：“Even so, employers complain they aren't given all the workers they need. The process is cumbersome, expensive, and unreliable. One survey found that bureaucratic delays led the average H-2A worker to arrive on the job 22 days late.” 农业雇主抱怨 H-2A 流程繁琐、昂贵且不可靠，官僚延误导致工人平均迟到22天，核心痛点在于签证审批手续过于缓慢，故选 [A] slow granting procedures。
［错项排除］[B] limit on duration of stay（逗留期限限制）来自第二段旧签证局限，非本段对 H-2A 抱怨；[C] tightened requirements（收紧申请条件）未提及；[D] control of annual admissions（年度配额控制）恰是 H-2B 签证的限制，原文明确指出“The H-2A visa has no numerical cap（H-2A 并无数量上限）”。

questions.stem: Which of the following could be the best title for this text?
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］主旨大意题（全文及末段）。
［解题思路］文章从美国农场面临的用工荒和移民制度障碍切入，剖析了本土工人不愿回流、机械化尚未成熟、H-2A 签证官僚拖延等困境，随之指出不少西部农场迁往墨西哥导致美国进口水果占比攀升，并在末段点明核心抉择：“In effect, the U.S. can import food or it can import the workers who pick it.”（实际上，美国要么进口食物，要么进口采摘食物的工人。）[B] Import Food or Labor? 凝练抓住了全篇灵魂，故选 [B]。
［错项排除］[A] U.S. Agriculture in Decline?（美国农业走向衰落？）过度拔高，问题在于劳动力短缺与供应链转移；[C] America Saved by Mexico?（美国被墨西哥拯救？）曲解农业迁往墨西哥与劳工来源；[D] Manpower vs. Automation?（人力与自动化之争？）仅涵盖第四段局部内容。

questions.stem: Some celebrities star in a new video to

options.text: demand new laws on the use of plastics
options.content: demand new laws on the use of plastics

options.text: urge consumers to cut the use of plastics
options.content: urge consumers to cut the use of plastics

options.text: invite public opinion on the plastics crisis
options.content: invite public opinion on the plastics crisis

options.text: disclose the causes of the plastics crisis
options.content: disclose the causes of the plastics crisis

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］事实细节题（考查多位明星出演世界环境日短片的目的）。

［解题思路］首段①②句指出，几位名人联袂出演世界环境日新短片——encouraging you, the consumer, to swap out your single-use plastic staples to combat the plastics crisis（鼓励消费者换掉日常一次性塑料制品，共同应对塑料危机）。可见其目的在于敦促消费者减少塑料制品的使用，故［B］urge consumers to cut the use of plastics 正确。

［错项排除］［A］第二段说明“呼吁政府立法”虽包含在环境日核心讯息中，但整体宣传重在针对个人消费者而非明星短片的主要目的；［C］“征求公众对塑料危机的意见”与短片“号召减少用塑”不符；［D］“揭露塑料危机成因”原文未提及，均排除。

questions.stem: The author is concerned that "moral licensing" may

options.text: mislead us into doing worthless things
options.content: mislead us into doing worthless things

options.text: prevent us from making further efforts
options.content: prevent us from making further efforts

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节理解题（第三段）。
［解题思路］第三段指出，自带购物袋或停用塑料吸管之所以可能带来危害，是因为这会满足人们觉得自己已经“尽了本分（done our bit）”的心理需求，却止步于此而不再推进更大、更大胆、更有效的变革行动——即所谓的“道德许可（moral licensing）”，它抚慰了我们的担忧并阻碍我们做更多事情及向当权者追责（allays our concerns and stops us doing more and asking more of those in charge）。选项 [B] prevent us from making further efforts 精准对应 stops us doing more，故选 [B]。
［错项排除］[A] mislead us into doing worthless things（误导做毫无价值的事）过度绝对化，作者指出这些举动收效微弱（accomplish little）而非完全无用；[C] weaken our sense of accomplishment 与原文“满足已尽力的感觉”相反；[D] suppress our desire for success 偷换了做更多环保行动与向政府问责的指向。

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］推理判断题（第四段）。
［解题思路］第四段指出，当环保讨论一直停留在购物袋和吸管上时，我们就忽视了权力平衡——那等于暗示我们作为“消费者（consumers）”只能靠可持续购物来承担责任，而不是作为“公民（citizens）”向政府和行业追责以推动真正的系统性变革（hold our governments and industries to account to push for real systemic change）。作者点出“公民”身份旨在呼吁公众敦促政府主导变革应对塑料危机，故选 [D] we should press our government to lead the combat。
［错项排除］[A] our focus should be shifted to community welfare（重心应转向社区福利）偏离环保问责；[B] our relationship with local industries is improving（与地方产业关系改善）与追责问效相悖；[C] we have been actively exercising our civil rights（一直在积极行使公民权利）时态与事实均与当前“忽视了作为公民去追责”相反。

questions.stem: DeSombre argues that the best way for a collective change should be
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］观点态度题（考查学者 DeSombre 主张的集体变革路径）。

［解题思路］第五段末句引述 Elizabeth R. DeSombre 指出，集体改变大众行为的最佳方式是结构性变革（for the change to be structural）；第六段紧接着具体说明何谓“结构性变革”——实施诸如塑料税（plastic tax）、全面禁止一次性塑料（banning single-use plastics altogether）及配套激励等公共政策。此类由政府政策与制度设计引领全局的路径，正属于［D］a top-down process（自上而下的推进过程），故［D］正确。

［错项排除］［A］“双赢安排”偏离政策驱动本义；［B］“自我驱动机制”与作者批判过度依赖个人自觉相悖；［C］“高性价比方法”原文未提及，故均排除。

questions.stem: The author concludes that individual efforts
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］观点结论题（第七、八段）。
［解题思路］第七段与第八段明确收束观点：“It's just that individual actions are too slow, she says, for that to be the only, or even primary, approach to changing widespread behavior. None of this is about writing off the individual... We don't have time to wait. We need progressive policies that shape collective action...” 作者并非全盘否定个人作用，但强调个体行动过于缓慢，作为唯一或主要手段远远不够（far from sufficient），亟需系统性政策牵引集体行动，故选 [C] are far from sufficient。
［错项排除］[A] can be too aggressive（可能过于激进）与温和微小的自带购物袋完全相反；[B] can be too inconsistent（可能太不一致）偏离时间紧迫、个体收效太慢的论据核心；[D] are far from rational（远非理性）并非作者对个人行动的定性。

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］人物观点匹配题（第十四至十五段）。
［解题思路］商业分析网站 FitSmallBusiness.com 的房产分析师 Julie Gurner 指出，父母应当提醒孩子需求与愿望会随时变化，“that decision should likely not be made contingent on a child's opinions, but rather made for them with great consideration into what home can meet their needs best”（买房决定不应取决于孩子的意见，而应立足于最能满足其长远需求的房屋来为他们做决定）。not contingent on opinions but meet needs 精确对应 [F] believes that homebuying decisions should be based on children's needs rather than their opinions，故选 [F]。
［错项排除］[D] 强调让孩子有参与感出自 Adam Bailey；[C] 强调不单纯依据孩子意见由 Tracey Hampson 提出，而 Gurner 明确对比了“需求（needs）”与“意见（opinions）”。
